purpose: The persistent source of truth for Umbrella project decisions. Its purpose is not to display notes; it is to make research and project selection compound.

umbrella_model.description: A portfolio and revenue lab that researches, builds or buys, improves, monetises, keeps, expands or sells assets, then feeds the lessons into the next decision.

sections.branded: Projects that publicly carry the Umbrella identity/face and are intended to strengthen visible reputation, audience, trust and ecosystem.
sections.unbranded: Standalone brands or quiet assets not publicly associated with Umbrella, including assets designed to be sold.

rules: Branding status must not bias the economic assessment of a project.
Early projects should prioritise learning while still pursuing real revenue.
Every project is a learning asset even when it is parked or sold.
Projects are assessed on their own economics, not because they fit the founder's existing trade or background.
A project may be kept, improved, expanded, sold or killed based on evidence.

mission.current: Find Project 1: the revenue-producing project with the strongest realistic odds of earning and teaching us useful lessons.
mission.preferred_outcome: A relatively low-cost asset that can create repeatable or increasingly automated revenue while leaving time and capital to pursue larger projects such as Buildalong.

decision_protocol: Retrieve existing intelligence relevant to the decision.
Identify what is already known and what remains unknown.
Research only the evidence gaps instead of restarting from generic idea lists.
Record findings, confidence, source type, implications and contradictions.
Score the opportunity using weighted criteria.
Choose the next experiment based on evidence rather than attachment.
Store the result so the next decision starts ahead of the previous one.

weighted_assessment.principle: Factors do not have equal influence. Revenue and realistic progress toward revenue outweigh learning value.

factors.name: Speed to first revenue
factors.reason: Early validation and cash flow reduce the cost of being wrong.

factors.name: Automation potential
factors.reason: The portfolio should increasingly create revenue without proportional manual effort.

factors.name: Traffic or demand potential
factors.reason: The project needs a realistic path to users or transactions.

factors.name: Scalability
factors.reason: Revenue should be able to grow faster than workload.

factors.name: Startup cost and complexity
factors.reason: Early experiments should be affordable and fast to test.

factors.name: Learning value
factors.reason: Useful, but it should not rescue a weak revenue opportunity.

weighted_assessment.score_rule: Score evidence quality separately from attractiveness. A high score with weak evidence remains unproven.

projects.name: SpecFlow
projects.original_hypothesis: A tool for web professionals to turn client discovery information into a clear project specification that can be sent to another company or used to guide a build.
why_started: Fast to build and test as a digital product.
Appeared to solve a real workflow problem around collecting requirements.
Provided a useful first learning project.
projects.revenue_assessment: The basic specification generator did not provide enough evidence of a strong revenue path. A generic document-generation layer is vulnerable to substitution by existing tools and general AI.
projects.stronger_hypothesis: Website project scope and requirement intelligence that identifies missing requirements, contradictions, ambiguity and scope risks before quoting or building.
lessons: A technically useful output is not automatically a monetisable product.
The intelligence layer may be more defensible than the formatted document.
A project should be parked when evidence is weak rather than defended because work has already been invested.
revisit_triggers: Strong evidence that agencies lose meaningful money to scope risk.
Evidence of willingness to pay for requirement or scope intelligence.

projects.name: Buildalong
projects.original_hypothesis: A builder-to-customer experience product that helps possible jobs, notes, progress and communication stay professional and simple.
projects.strategic_role: Potential larger project with more development and capital requirements. It is not the project that must fund the entire journey from day one.
projects.audience_principle: The builder pays because the customer's experience is valuable.
projects.current_position: Future project; revenue-building projects should help create time, money and learning for it.

projects.name: Project 1 Search
projects.objective: Find the strongest evidence-backed revenue-producing digital asset without limiting the search to SaaS, apps, websites or direct customer payments.
selection_rules: Money mechanism must be identifiable before serious development.
Existing demand is preferred over trying to manufacture demand.
The project should be testable quickly and killable without large sunk cost.
Traffic alone is not enough; the path from activity to revenue must be explicit.
Do not choose an idea simply because it is easy to build.
Do not choose an idea simply because it matches a familiar trade or industry.
projects.current_stage: Narrow niche validation. Broad opportunity models remain open; generic heat-pump grant tools and generic car fault-code lookups have been deprioritised due to visible competition.

projects.name: Umbrella Intelligence
projects.objective: Store and retrieve research, decisions, evidence, failures and lessons so every project improves the next one.
projects.critical_requirement: The intelligence must be usable in future decision-making, not merely visible in a dashboard.

confirmed_lessons.title: Revenue creation is the goal
confirmed_lessons.detail: A project can earn through subscriptions, one-off sales, advertising, affiliate commission, referrals, lead generation, asset sales or other mechanisms. Direct payment by the user is optional.

confirmed_lessons.title: Existing demand is an advantage
confirmed_lessons.detail: Prefer projects that capture a need people already express through searches, buying intent or repeated workflows.

confirmed_lessons.title: Buildability is not viability
confirmed_lessons.detail: A product can be easy to create and still have weak demand, distribution or monetisation.

confirmed_lessons.title: Traffic must connect to money
confirmed_lessons.detail: High traffic is not automatically valuable. The revenue mechanism and visitor intent matter.

confirmed_lessons.title: Projects should be easy to test and easy to kill
confirmed_lessons.detail: Early experiments should produce evidence before large amounts of time or money are committed.

confirmed_lessons.title: Research must compound
confirmed_lessons.detail: Before new research, retrieve what we already know and focus on missing evidence.

confirmed_lessons.title: Economics outrank attachment
confirmed_lessons.detail: A project can be kept, expanded, sold, parked or killed based on evidence rather than effort already invested.

confirmed_lessons.title: The portfolio can learn across categories
confirmed_lessons.detail: Lessons about demand, monetisation, traffic, automation and distribution can transfer between apps, sites, tools and assets.

confirmed_lessons.title: Reputation can compound, but branding is optional
confirmed_lessons.detail: The Branded can strengthen trust and traffic; The Unbranded can operate independently or be built for sale. Neither gets an automatic economic advantage.

opportunity_fields.name: High-intent lead generation
opportunity_fields.model: Capture people already seeking a valuable service and connect them with providers.
strengths: Users may not need to pay
Revenue can be tied to transaction value
opportunity_fields.current_assessment: Very high interest; needs niche-by-niche evidence.

opportunity_fields.name: Free useful tool → revenue engine
opportunity_fields.model: Give immediate value through a calculator, checker, estimator, generator, converter or lookup, then monetise relevant intent.
strengths: No requirement for users to pay
risks: Generic tools may struggle to rank
Monetisation must fit the exact user moment
opportunity_fields.current_assessment: Very high interest; strong candidate if a narrow demand gap is found.

opportunity_fields.name: Niche comparison / directory
opportunity_fields.model: Help users decide between suppliers, products, services or options and monetise the decision journey.
strengths: Can grow into a data asset
risks: Thin or generic directories have weak differentiation
opportunity_fields.current_assessment: High interest; niche selection is critical.

opportunity_fields.name: Automated information / data asset
opportunity_fields.model: Collect, organise and maintain useful structured information that people struggle to search or compare.
strengths: Can create many useful entry points
risks: Information alone is not enough without a useful interface
opportunity_fields.current_assessment: High interest; potentially slower to first revenue.

opportunity_fields.name: Digital products and repeatable assets
opportunity_fields.model: Create once, sell repeatedly or use the asset to support other revenue mechanisms.
opportunity_fields.current_assessment: Open; only pursue where demand and distribution are clear.

opportunity_fields.name: Buy → improve → profit → keep or sell
opportunity_fields.model: Acquire undervalued products or digital assets, improve their economics or presentation, then retain or sell.
strengths: Creates real-world pricing and operational learning
opportunity_fields.current_assessment: Long-term portfolio path; not necessarily the first zero-cost project.

rejected_or_parked_patterns.reason: A thin layer over broadly available AI can be easy to substitute unless it owns a specific workflow, data advantage or distribution channel.
This repeats the SpecFlow risk. The path from user activity to revenue should be identified before serious development.

rejected_or_parked_patterns.pattern: Generic idea lists as final evidence
rejected_or_parked_patterns.reason: Lists are useful for discovery but do not prove demand, distribution, economics or competitive opportunity.
Attention is not enough when visitors have no natural next action that creates revenue.
The portfolio should search for economics and opportunity across categories rather than forcing every project into bricklaying or trades.

research_queue.task: Find narrow opportunities where existing high-intent demand and a direct monetisation path meet.
research_queue.output: Ranked evidence-backed candidates with explicit money mechanism and traffic route.

research_queue.task: For each candidate, identify the exact user moment and current workaround.
research_queue.output: Proof that the project solves or captures an existing behaviour.

research_queue.task: Assess competitors and identify whether a real gap exists.
research_queue.output: Reason to build rather than copy.
A V1 experiment designed to prove or disprove the revenue theory quickly.

research_log.question: Can high-intent free tools and lead-generation assets produce stronger Project 1 candidates than generic software?

findings.candidate: Generic UK heat-pump / grant eligibility checker
findings.verdict: Too crowded as a default Project 1 choice
findings.evidence: Multiple dedicated checkers, calculators and installer lead funnels already exist; recent government grant changes create demand but also attract fast competition.
findings.implication: Do not build a generic checker. Only revisit if a narrow underserved audience or distribution advantage is identified.

findings.evidence: Large free code libraries and several newer UK-focused explainers already cover plain-English code meanings, costs and repair guidance.
findings.implication: A simple code database is not enough. A future automotive asset would need a stronger data, workflow or transaction layer.

findings.verdict: Still attractive at the model level
findings.evidence: Current lead-generation reporting and UK service advertising benchmarks indicate that qualified service enquiries have measurable commercial value, while users can receive the service for free.
findings.implication: Continue niche-by-niche research rather than abandoning the model.

findings.verdict: Potentially attractive but niche selection is decisive
findings.evidence: Comparison and broker sites already compete heavily in obvious verticals such as business energy.
findings.implication: Avoid entering broad established comparison markets without a sharply differentiated user problem.

research_log.new_rule: A current trend or new government incentive is not enough by itself. We must separately prove demand, monetisation and that the exact version we build is not already commoditised.

project_1_candidates.name: Pre-Purchase Property Risk Checker
project_1_candidates.one_line: A free address-based checker that tells a UK buyer which specialist property checks are worth considering before exchange, then earns from introductions to relevant surveyors.
project_1_candidates.revenue: Qualified surveyor introductions, pay-per-lead, affiliate/referral agreements.
project_1_candidates.why: One user can create multiple high-value downstream services; the product can start narrow and expand into a property-intelligence asset.
project_1_candidates.risk: Property data accuracy and strong comparison-site competition; must begin with a narrow, useful decision layer rather than pretending to be a full legal search.

project_1_candidates.name: Build-Over & Drain Risk Checker
project_1_candidates.one_line: A free postcode-and-project checker for homeowners planning extensions who need to understand whether public sewers or drainage constraints could affect the build, with routes to surveys and specialist help.
project_1_candidates.why: Clear project trigger, high commercial intent, and a concrete next action.
project_1_candidates.risk: Water-company rules and maps vary; exact property-level answers require careful data handling.

project_1_candidates.name: Specialist Survey Decision Tool
project_1_candidates.one_line: A guided free tool for UK home buyers that converts visible property concerns and survey findings into a prioritised answer about whether a roof, damp, drainage, structural, asbestos or other specialist survey is worth getting.
project_1_candidates.why: The decision problem is broader and more useful than a single quote form and can create multiple monetisable outcomes.
project_1_candidates.risk: Must avoid giving professional diagnoses; start with clear guidance and evidence-backed triggers.

project_1_candidates.name: Renovation Compliance & Requirements Checker
project_1_candidates.one_line: Enter an address and planned works to receive a plain-English checklist of likely permissions, constraints and specialist checks before spending money.
project_1_candidates.revenue: Introductions to surveyors, designers, specialists and relevant services.
project_1_candidates.why: Large umbrella opportunity with many possible revenue branches and strong learning value.
project_1_candidates.risk: Broad scope and fragmented official data; must start with one tightly defined renovation journey.

project_1_candidates.name: Home Survey Follow-Up Decoder
project_1_candidates.one_line: Upload or paste the recommendations from a home survey and receive a structured list of what needs a specialist follow-up, what is urgent, and what type of professional to contact.
project_1_candidates.revenue: Qualified introductions to surveyors and specialists.
project_1_candidates.why: Users already have an expensive purchase underway and are close to spending money.
project_1_candidates.risk: Document parsing quality and safety; should initially classify survey recommendations rather than diagnose the property.

project_selection_principles.rule: Do not constrain opportunity research to problem-solving products.
project_selection_principles.meaning: Project 1 research must begin with the objective of finding the strongest realistic route to revenue and asset value, not with an assumption that the answer must be an app, SaaS, useful tool, or problem solver.
search_order: Existing money flows we can capture or redirect
Assets we can buy or build cheaply and improve
Transactions where commission, referral or brokerage revenue is possible
Digital products with proven existing demand
Traffic or attention assets with realistic monetisation
project_selection_principles.guardrail: Every serious candidate should be compared against opportunities from other revenue mechanisms before commitment. A clever or useful idea does not receive preference merely because it is a product we can build.
